t: Convert Doubly Linked List to Array II
o: You are handed an arbitrary node of a doubly linked list, not necessarily the head. Walk `prev` pointers until you reach the head, then walk `next` pointers collecting values. With at most 500 nodes, anything linear is fine.
k: A doubly linked list lets you reach the head from any node by following prev until it is null.
Once at the head, a standard forward traversal collects the values in order.

a.n: Approach 1: Walk back to head, then forward
a.i: Two simple pointer walks: rewind to the head, then collect values going forward.
s: While node.prev exists, move node = node.prev
Traverse from head via next, appending values
a.t: O(n) — each pointer is followed once

a.i: Find the head recursively, then build the array with recursion on `next` — same complexity, just a different style.
s: Recursively append node.val then recurse on node.next
a.sp: O(n) recursion stack in the worst case

w: Both approaches are equivalent; prefer the iterative one in interviews (no stack-depth concerns). Edge cases: the given node is already the head, or a single-node list. Follow-up: could you do it with O(1) passes if you were only given `next` pointers? You couldn't reach the head at all — that's why the list is doubly linked.
